disclaimer: Heuristic static checks run against the host application's own classes only, plus a survey of which dependencies ship reachability metadata. They complement, but do not replace, the GraalVM tracing agent and an actual native-image build and runtime tests. The scan does not determine whether imported calls execute or whether existing framework hints cover them.

dockerfile.content:
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for a GraalVM native image of app.
#
# This scaffold was generated by BootUI for the application the starter is installed in.
# It assumes a single-module Spring Boot application built with the Maven Wrapper and the `native` profile that spring-boot-starter-parent provides.
#
# Requires GraalVM 25+ for Spring Boot 4 (GraalVM 25 = JDK 25).
#
# Build and run (publish the port with -p so the app is reachable from the host;
# EXPOSE alone does not publish it):
#   docker build -f Dockerfile-native -t app .
#   docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 app

# Build stage with GraalVM 25 (includes the native-image toolchain, JDK 25)
FROM ghcr.io/graalvm/graalvm-community:25 AS build

WORKDIR /app

# Copy the project (see .dockerignore for exclusions).
COPY . .

# Make the Maven Wrapper executable.
RUN chmod +x mvnw

# Request a "mostly static" executable using the documented public option.
# Depending on the application, libstdc++/libgcc or dynamically loaded native
# libraries may still be needed. Inspect the executable's dependencies with ldd
# and exercise it in the final image before relying on this scaffold.
# NATIVE_IMAGE_OPTIONS affects this container build, not local host builds.
ENV NATIVE_IMAGE_OPTIONS="--static-nolibc"

# Build the native executable. This runs Spring Boot's AOT processing, downloads the
# GraalVM reachability metadata and then compiles the native image.
RUN ./mvnw -Pnative -DskipTests clean native:compile

# Move the native executable to a known path (named after the module/project, i.e. app).
RUN if [ -f target/app ]; then \
      cp target/app native-app; \
    else \
      native_exe=$(find target -maxdepth 1 -type f -executable ! -name '*.jar' ! -name '*.jar.original' | head -1) && \
      if [ -n "$native_exe" ]; then cp "$native_exe" native-app; \
      else echo "ERROR: Native executable not found"; ls -laR target | head -40; exit 1; fi; \
    fi

# Runtime stage: Google "distroless" base. It ships glibc (and the dynamic loader) but
# no shell or package manager. It is a starting point, not a guarantee that all
# application-specific native libraries are present. If the executable needs
# libstdc++/libgcc, consider distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot or another compatible
# runtime. The :nonroot tag runs as an unprivileged user (uid 65532).
FROM gcr.io/distroless/base-debian12:nonroot

WORKDIR /app

# Copy the native executable from the build stage
COPY --from=build --chown=nonroot:nonroot /app/native-app native-app

USER nonroot

EXPOSE 8080

# No Docker HEALTHCHECK: the distroless base has no shell or curl to run a probe. Probe
# the web server (or /actuator/health) from your orchestrator's liveness/readiness
# checks instead.

# Run the native application
ENTRYPOINT ["./native-app"]
dockerfile.installPath: The application is not running from an exploded build (for example a packaged jar), so there is no project directory to write into.
